recipes.name: Fresh Rhubarb Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients, and preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place an oven rack in the lowest position.
Line the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate with one pie crust. Combine sugar and flour in a small bowl; sprinkle 1/4 of the sugar mixture over the prepared bottom crust.
Heap chopped rhubarb on top and sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture. Dot with butter and cover with top crust.
Bake pie in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until filling is bubbly and crust is golden brown, about 40 to 45 minutes.
Serve the pie warm or cold. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Rhubarb Pie
raw_recipe.description: This rhubarb pie is made with fresh rhubarb and easy pantry ingredients for a luscious sweet and tangy filling inside a golden double-crust pie.

review.reviewBody: Don't bother with the butter; you don't need it at all. And do NOT--as some other reviewers have suggested--mix up the flour/sugar mixture with the fruit before adding the fruit to the pie shell. The reason you want copious amounts of sugar both on the bottom and on the top of the fruit (rather than mixed amongst it) is that while baking, the bubbling-hot sugar carmelizes in contact with the bottom and top crusts, a process which makes the crusts rather crispy in the final product. If you mix the sugar up with the fruit, you don't get that crispy crust, and the large amount of water in the rhubarb will definitely make the bottom crust sodden. Don't worry: the sugar makes its way through the fruit anyway, so you won't have parts of the pie too sweet and other parts too tart.

I won $100 for 1st prize in a rhubarb pie baking contest with this recipe. The only thing I did different, since I used green rhubarb, was tint the sugar with 2 drops of red food coloring before adding the flour. I also sprinkled a little sugar on top the crust. I used Pie Crust I from this site.
Update 5/20/07
I won the rhubarb pie contest and the $100 prize again yesterday with this recipe. Since I made a 10 inch pie, I used 5 cups rhubarb, 1 2/3 cups sugar, 7 1/2 T flour, and 1 T butter. I added 3 drops red food color to the sugar. This pie is definitely a winner!

This was fabulous. I did make some little changes tho--I upped the rhubarb per pie to 6cups (could have done fine with 8 I think), kept sugar at 1 1/3 cup, upped the flour by half for a non-running pie...added 1 tsp cinnamon to the flour/sugar mix, and a few drops of vanilla to the pie all around, before baking..milk and sugar on top before baking made a flaky, crispy top crust--gosh but the kids LOVED THIS, so did the husband...out of vanilla ice cream so used some RediWhip instead. Did 2 of these today, but next time I'll do 3 or 4 on one day. SUPER RECIPE, THANKS!

I made this pie using fresh rhubarb and Splenda sugar (used only 1 cup of splenda) and it turned out GREAT!!! I brushed the pie crust with egg and sprinkled lightly with white sugar and it looked as pretty as it tasted! This is definately a keeper!

Turned out perfect. My teens loved it. I mixed in 1 1/2 cups frozen mixed berries because I was afraid the rhubarb would be too tart. I think it would have been fine without the berries. I also added 1/2 t. of vanilla to the sugar/flour mix. If you let it cool before slicing, it's not soupy. Thanks for the great recipe!

I painted the bottom crust with egg whites so that the crust wouldn’t get soggy. As I had some left I used it to “glue” the two crusts together and then used som on the top crust as well and sprinkled it with Sugar in the Raw.

This recipe was the best! Everyone loved it and it reminded all who ate it of the one's "my grandma made" What I did differently was I used 5 cups rhubarb, extra teaspoon of flour. I put 1/4 of the sugar and flour mixture on the bottom, mixed 1/2 into rhubarb with an 1/8 teaspoon of cinnamon (not to overpower just trying), and the rest of sugar flour mixture on top. This was literally to die for!! Will definitely be making again,. When I have rhubarb that is.

When I made this recipe, I added 6 drops of red food coloring to the sugar. I also added one pound of strawberries and 2 Tbs of tapioca to help thicken the pie, due to the liquid from the strawberries. I made a bottom crust and a crumble for the top. It turned out to be a beautiful red and extremely delicious!! It was also quick and easy to make. I have looked for many, many years to find a rhubarb pie recipe that is PERFECT! I can now stop my search. I have found the recipe I have been looking for. It's a keeper for sure. Thank you for sharing this recipe.? I love it!

I'd give it almost 5 stars. The recipe is so simple, and it makes a yummy pie. The first time I made it, I followed the recipe, and it was too sweet. The second time I made it, I used less sugar, and it was better. I used frozen rhubarb, which I thawed, and pre-baked the bottom pie crust to make sure it cooked and was not going to be soggy. I was so happy to find out how easy this pie was to make and how yummy it was because it is so hard to find already-made rhubarb pies anywhere! It is my favorite :) I will be making this again and again. Thank you so much!

I am so impressed. I have never been able to make a rhubarb pie without it turning into soup. I followed the recipe but also added 1/4 c sugar to rhubarb before filling pie and put in fridge to draw out the water for 4 hours (tip from my Better Hones cookbook that is 50 years old). I waited for pie to cool off but I couldn’t wait so when still warm I sliced. It and wow amazing it wasn’t runny and it was so delish.

Made for my son, I didn't get to taste it but, I heard he ate 3 slices in a row! I think it's worth 5 stars. I added strawberries to get it up to 5 cups for a 10-inch pie, reduced the sugar to 1 cup, increased the flour/sugar by just a bit. I didn't want to have a runny pie. I used "French Pie Crust" on this site which is always a winner. I'm sure to make this one again.
This recipe is soooo easy to make. It’s absolutely fantastic.

It was an excellent recipe! I added orange zest and nutmeg to my recipe, and I added 2 tablespoons of butter instead of one. I also made a lattice crust, that I added an egg wash to. I then sprinkled sugar and cinnamon on top and it was heavenly! I served it warm with vanilla bean ice cream. And it was a huge hit. There wasn’t a piece left in the pie pan.

I just put my second pie in the oven. Follow the recipe to a T — I forgot the butter last time, but it was still delicious. I got a store-bought crust this time. The first one was really good, but it was too much work! I cut down on the sugar a little bit (a heaping cup) because I want more tart rhubarb flavor this time, and at the very end, there was a little bit of un melted sugar right beneath the air holes in the crust. (just a few drops of water, took care of that.) I did a little less heaping with the rhubarb in the center of the pie plate that I did last time. I’m hoping that it comes ok.

I just don't understand what was supposed to happen with the pile of flour/sugar on top because it just sat there in a pile throughout the cooking process. Once pie was cooled, I cut into it and tried eating it but the big hard white chunks were too crunchy and I don't care for the taste of flour/sugar in chunks. I've made many pies in my life but none have ever been this level of disaster.
I made the recipe with no changes. Got rave reviews! Super easy to make!

The only thing I did different was only used 1 cup sugar and an extra Tbs of flour. This is a great pie and super easy!! As you can see by the picture, there was no bubbling overflow, but use a sheet pan to catch the few drips.

My rhubarb wasn’t forced and was actually quite woody. I was really worried that this wasn’t gunna turn out because not only was it my first rhubarb pie, but my first pie in general. My goodness!! Took this to a games night with my pals and every plate was licked clean. Thanks so much!!!
Very easy to make & tasty
I used a crumble topping and it was delicious. Thank you for the recipe
